answers.answer: Roll one die for each held office card simultaneously, adding one for each fatigue on that card; the Chairman also adds one. A modified result of 1–2 does nothing, 3–4 adds fatigue, and 5+ retires the member. Move the retiring member to Pensioners, flip the office card into Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to the supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make normal office attrition rolls.
answers.evidence: London Season—Attrition: ‘Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire.’

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner may take or discard one card from the London Season display. They act in descending order of their actual total retirement spending. Ties go first to the player with the most total windows, counting new prizes, then clockwise from the Prime Minister. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Cards are not replaced immediately; if the display is empty, skip remaining eligible players. At the end, discard every card still displayed and refill exactly three cards—prestige faceup and blackmail facedown—even if nobody took a card. Return all unused pensioners to their supplies.
answers.evidence: London Season—Prestige: ‘descending actual total retirement spending. Ties: most total windows … then clockwise from PM.’

answers.answer: In Family, players act starting with the Chairman and then clockwise. Each takes one chosen family action and places their opportunity marker on it. If the marker was already on that action at phase start, that action may be taken twice. Only the latest passed extra-action law is usable; its extra action is not doubled by the marker and does not move the marker. With at least four vacant offices, Enlist Writer places one additional writer once that turn. Thus, if the opportunity marker was already on Enlist Writer, the doubled action places two writers and the vacancy bonus adds one, for three writers total.
answers.evidence: Family: ‘If your marker was already on that action at phase start, you may take that action twice’; Enlist Writer bonus is ‘once this turn.’

answers.answer: After all family actions, if the Company has Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one; repeat while both Debt and applicants remain. Pieces in Court are Company shares. If no Debt remains, slide the remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. The initial price paid when seeking a share goes to the bank; it is not paid into a Company treasury.
answers.evidence: New Company shares: ‘move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one’; seeking a share ‘never pays family cash into Company treasuries.’

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending order of the number on the backs of their cards. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that member into the office, and the member’s owner receives the office card. When promoting an officeholder, move that office’s fatigue to the new card and put the old card, now vacant, into the ascending hiring order. Ordinary hiring of a member from the hirer’s own family requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. If there is no candidate or the hirer is vacant, skip that office: it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring: ‘Fill vacant offices in ascending number’; Nepotism requires consent of ‘every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool.’

answers.answer: The former Chairman announces a pure majority of current Company shares, meaning more than half. Shareholders may campaign, and the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner’s Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. That piece continues to count as a share for dividends, majority calculations, and scoring, but it cannot be traded or invested in a firm. If no candidate gets majority support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. If the Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if needed and possible, taking one from a prize and losing its VP. If return is impossible, there is no Chairman.
answers.evidence: Chairman election: ‘pure majority of current shares (more than half)’; a Chairman share ‘cannot be traded or invested in firms.’

answers.answer: Before a Company-office check, commit the required resources and cash; all cash for such a check comes from that acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll. Use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails but may be retried if resources and that office’s limits permit; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that officeholder’s further actions, returns the officeholder to supply, discards their fatigue, and flips the office card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures can modify this general procedure. Do not take an action that has no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying without dice merely to trigger possible officer losses.
answers.evidence: Success checks: ‘Use lowest die: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure, retry if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 catastrophic failure.’

answers.answer: The Chairman may voluntarily add up to three Debt, receiving £5 Balance for each, without consent. Each advance beyond those three requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman. The Chairman may never advance Debt past the Debt track’s end. They must allocate all Company Balance to other offices’ treasuries, reducing Balance by the amount of each transfer; they may interleave borrowing and allocation while observing the borrowing limits. Money already in office treasuries remains there for those offices to use.
answers.evidence: Chairman: ‘May add up to three Debt freely, each +£5 Balance’; then ‘allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries.’

answers.answer: The Manager of Shipping must spend from that office’s treasury until £2 or less remains. They may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the shipyard owner’s consent, and buy a Company ship for £5 only when no ships remain on shipyards. Each acquired ship goes into any sea zone, including China if that office exists. Leased extra ships serve only until Refresh.
answers.evidence: Manager of Shipping: ‘Must spend treasury until £2 or less remains’; Company ship purchase is allowed ‘only if no ships remain on shipyards.’

answers.answer: A President declares the regions for a Trade action. The declaration must include that Presidency’s home region and may include only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President’s treasury buys one die; subtract one die for every declared nonhome region. A failed check can be retried during that President’s operations if affordable; catastrophe removes the President. Each President can have at most one successful Trade per turn. Failed attempts and retries are part of that President’s uninterrupted opportunity, so another position cannot act between them. On success, fill one order per ship in its sea zone, as many as possible within declared regions: the first writer goes to the home port, and each following order must be adjacent to one already filled by this Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President cannot fill another Presidency’s home region, even if that office is vacant. Add each order’s printed value to Company Balance, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn under Deregulation. The President receives £1 from the bank per order, and owners receive £1 per writer placed. Use dividers to separate adjacent writers belonging to different Presidencies so they return correctly at Refresh.
answers.evidence: Presidency Trade: ‘include home region’; ‘subtract one per declared nonhome region’; at most ‘one successful Trade per President per turn.’

answers.answer: A Commander may target their Presidency’s home region, any region associated with that Presidency, or any region bordering an associated region. They may not target another Presidency’s home region or a Company-controlled region associated with another Presidency. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for the action to have an effect. Exhaust selected officers and regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed number of dice. Subtract the combined strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once; Company-controlled defense strength is zero. Roll the normal check, and a noncatastrophic failure may be retried with remaining resources. After every attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll officer-loss dice.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: allowed targets include own home/associated/bordering regions; ‘After each attempt’ officers roll for losses.

answers.answer: On a successful Deploy, loot is £4 per tower in the target plus the faceup loot token modifier, with a minimum of one plus the number of surviving officers used. Distribute £1 to the Commander plus £1 per surviving officer they used; clockwise, give £1 to each other player per surviving officer they used; then pay £1 to the bank per regiment and per local-alliance piece, regardless of alliance strength, repeating the cycle until the loot is exhausted. The Commander gains one trophy per target tower. For control, remove the target tower and dome; if it was a capital, remove all matching empire flags. Open all its orders and clear its unrest. If the target becomes Company-controlled, put its loot/control token region-side above the President, place a Governor overlay, and add the office card to vacancies. If the Elephant is in a conquered region and points outward, place it fully inside. On catastrophic failure, the Commander returns half their family’s trophies, rounded up, and their member to supply; exhausted officers still make their loss checks. A Commander has no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Successful Deploy: ‘loot = £4 per target tower + faceup loot token’s modifier’; catastrophe returns half the Commander family’s trophies rounded up.

answers.answer: A Governor uses their printed dice pool, makes repeated attempts with no penalty, and reduces the pool by one after every result. On success, the Governor receives £1, plus another £1 if the previous roll was unsuccessful, and chooses one benefit: build a Company ship (first place a partially built ship in the Governor’s region; a later success completes it into the sea zone associated with that Presidency); commission a regiment into that Presidency’s Army; or tax, adding an unsplit £2 to Balance or that President’s treasury. Every Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Every unsuccessful check also adds unrest. The Governor may continue until choosing to stop, having no dice, or suffering catastrophe; catastrophe follows normal office removal.
answers.evidence: Governors—Administer: ‘reduce pool one after every result’; each unsuccessful check adds unrest; each Tax after first adds unrest.

answers.answer: During Company revenue, pay expenses by reducing Balance £1 for each existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in a sea zone, including China; exclude Commanders. If funds are insufficient, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one at a time to the track end, and continue receiving emergency loans even at maximum Debt. Newly added emergency Debt creates no additional expense this turn. After emergency loans, set Balance to zero. Taking one or two loans lowers Standing one; taking three or more lowers it two. Then compare the remaining Balance with the expectations under current Standing; if Balance is lower, lower Standing one. Next the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, costing £1 per Company share and paying £1 per share to each owner, including the Chairman. If total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than current expectations, advance Standing one. Reaching the leftmost Standing space causes Company failure.
answers.evidence: Revenue—Expenses/Expectations/Dividends: emergency loans ‘continue … even at maximum Debt’; expectations are checked before dividends.

answers.answer: For an Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region, first resolve the primary attack, then secondary Rebellions in every other Company region that has unrest. Resolve those secondary attacks in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order; within each Presidency its Commander orders the attacks. For a normal Crisis, primary strength uses the normal attack calculation plus local unrest; a Foreign Invasion uses the ordinary die for attack strength without adding unrest to primary strength. An Invasion Crisis compares the attacker’s whole empire strength plus event modifier against the defender’s whole empire strength and succeeds only if strictly greater; a Rebellion compares only the rebelling region’s strength plus modifier against its sovereign capital’s strength, also requiring strictly greater. For attacks on Company regions, the associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling the attack strength, or as much as possible; local alliances use their printed strength and cannot be split. If newly exhausted strength is insufficient, the region is lost. Otherwise clear all unrest in the region and the Commander takes one trophy. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in their stead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses defense pieces and gets no trophies. This does not appoint a Commander. If the primary Invasion fails, remove one tower from the attacker if possible; on success apply the empire growth rules.
answers.evidence: Attacks on Company: ‘Resolve primary first; then Bombay, Madras, Bengal’; sufficient defense clears unrest and earns one trophy.

answers.answer: A vote result of −1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve any dilemma’s If Failed text, and have the Opposition Leader return the token and take the PM dial. The new PM moves the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. A result of zero or more passes: place the law among passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy, then resolve the law’s immediate effects. After either result, restore every card used for voting to its regular orientation. If the law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring. A support-zero vote passes because zero is sufficient. The supplied summary does not specify a separate support-zero exception to the ordinary pass rule.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Resolution: ‘−1 or less fails’; ‘Zero or higher passes’; selected policy resolves before immediate law effects.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. On passage, lower Debt by one for every two current Debt, reset Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. On failure, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, to a maximum of ±3. This vote has no policy; failure does not remove the PM or discard the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against it. The 1813 scenario starts deregulated. The special session is distinct from ordinary law voting and is checked at turn start before London Season.
answers.evidence: Deregulation: PM ‘may’ call when on lined space and ‘must’ when on starred space; failure neither removes PM nor discards the law.

answers.answer: In the Firms phase after Family share creation and before Hiring, players may form or invest in firms until no one wishes to act. To form a firm, a player not already managing one returns an eligible Company share to supply or flips a workshop to its invested side, flips their family board, places a family member as the first firm share, sets firm value to the leftmost space, and takes £5 from the bank into the London treasury. To invest, the manager must consent; the contributor uses the same Company-share or workshop contribution and the firm receives £5 from the bank into London for a new firm share. Investments after the ten-share cap still contribute £5 but create no share. A Chairman share cannot be used; Company shares cannot be invested at all if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space; and shares created that turn cannot be used, even if traded away. An invested workshop never returns to uninvested status and gives neither its normal bonus nor Company-failure VP; it remains invested if the firm fails. Family cash cannot move into or out of firm treasuries except via specified procedures. The Chairman share also cannot be traded or invested. Firm shares are tradable like Company shares.
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Form/Invest: creation uses an eligible Company share or workshop; the firm takes £5 from the bank into London.

answers.answer: Each firm manager secretly chooses a sea zone/home port and a London-treasury cash bid; a firm needs at least one ship to choose a zone. A closed home port does not prevent choosing it. Alternatively choose Hobnob with no bid: it does not trade or pay dividends, still has expenses, and retains its prior dividend marker for retirement. Reveal bids simultaneously but keep strategy cards facedown until the matching Presidency begins. At the start of that Presidency, before any actions, reveal matching strategies and roll one die per bid pound, paying the bid to the bank. At least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Initiative is ship count minus the number of successful dice (1s/2s), and can be negative. A successfully trading President gets initiative using its ships the same way. After the President succeeds, fill orders in ascending initiative; the President chooses among tied traders, so the Company is not automatically first. If the President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commanders/Governors have had a chance, with the Chairman deciding initiative ties. Each firm has one trade attempt per turn and fills up to ships plus one open orders, starting at its strategy home port and tracing its own route back to that port. It can fill each order only once. It may refill orders already filled by another firm or the Company that turn, and the Company may refill a firm’s order. Such previously filled orders pay half their printed revenue, rounded down. Firm revenue goes to its India treasury. Increase firm Value one space for each full £6 added to India that turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies: at least one bid die of 1/2 permits trade; initiative equals ships minus successful dice; refilled orders pay half rounded down.

answers.answer: At the start of Revenue, before Company revenue, firms pay expenses in initiative order, then other firms, with ties resolved by the manager with most windows and then PM clockwise order. Each owes £1 per charter ship plus the higher of its share count or firm Value. It may use either or both treasuries. If it cannot pay, it dissolves unless rescued. Dissolution sends its shares to Debtor’s Prison, costing each share −1 VP; ships return to shipyards; its charter returns to the family side; and invested workshops remain invested. For rescue, emergency investments follow normal Company-share/workshop rules, even if the ten-share cap means no additional shares; pay expenses, lose remaining cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment. Alternatively merge with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if it has not already done so and cover the endangered firm’s unpaid expenses. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends only from the India treasury. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share and £1 to the manager. With the manager’s consent, a shareholder can forgo payment for any number of shares on any dividend. Record the total actual cash paid as dividends on the Company Balance track. An active non-Hobnob firm paying no dividend records zero; Hobnob retains its previous marker. Sweep remaining India money into London.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses/rescue/dividends: expense is ‘£1 per charter ship plus higher of share count or firm value’; dividends come from India treasury only.
